[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#executive-summary]

## Executive Summary

Portal Studio embeds product domain UI **Modules** as **Webpack 5 Module Federation remotes**. The Portal Studio shell (Next.js) is the MF host; each Module is an MF exposed entry that publishes a `remoteEntry.js` to JFrog and declares its URL in `studio-manifest.json`. This pattern defines how a product domain repository organizes, builds, and publishes its Portal Studio Modules as one or more **Product Packages** (`@mmes/{domain}-{package-name}-studio-webpack`) each with a shared `studio-manifest.json`.

---
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#context-and-problem]

## Context and Problem

Portal Studio's import UI discovers Modules by reading `studio-manifest.json` from published npm packages in the `@mmes` JFrog registry. Without a defined pattern, each product team independently decides:

- Whether to publish one package per Module or one per repo
- How to name MF remotes and Module namespaces
- Where to store the manifest and `remoteEntry.js`
- How to wire locale strings and design tokens
- How to build a dev harness without a running Portal Studio instance

This leads to inconsistent registration, namespace collisions across domains, and broken MF composition.

---
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#solution]

## Solution

**One package per concern group (default: one per repo).** A `@mmes/{product}-{package-name}-studio-webpack` npm package contains all Portal Studio Modules for a concern group. Each Module is a Webpack 5 MF exposed entry; the package produces a single Module Bundle (`remoteEntry.js`) that exposes all Modules. A `studio-manifest.json` at the package root lists all Modules in a `modules[]` array, each with its `remoteEntry` URL and `exposedModule` name.

A domain may publish multiple packages if concern groups have independent release cadences — the granularity is a domain team decision. See [STD-APP-COMP-001 §1.2](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#12-terminology) for the full hierarchy.

This pattern is enforced by [STD-APP-COMP-001](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md) and scaffolded by `/ui-component-create` in the `eap-bootstrap` developer harness.

---
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#package-structure]

## Package Structure

```
components/react/packages/{package-name}/      ← package root
├── src/modules/{ModuleName}/                  ← module source
├── studio/
│   ├── studio-manifest.json                   ← ONE manifest, modules[] array (schemaVersion: "1.0")
│   ├── package.json                           ← @mmes/{product}-{package-name}-studio-webpack
│   └── webpack.mf.config.js                   ← Webpack 5 MF build config (Module Bundle)
├── dist/
│   └── mf/
│       ├── remoteEntry.js                     ← Module Bundle (built output, gitignored)
│       └── *.js                               ← lazy-loaded Module chunks
└── components/
    ├── <module-name>/                         ← module source
    │   ├── src/                               ← implementation (React component)
    │   │   └── <ModuleName>.tsx
    │   ├── dist/                              ← ESM build (library consumers, Vite)
    │   ├── test/
    │   │   └── harness.html                   ← standalone dev harness (loads remoteEntry.js)
    │   ├── vite.config.ts                     ← ESM library build only (not Module Bundle)
    │   └── webpack.mf.config.cjs              ← delegates to bundle-level config
    └── module-demo/                           ← multi-tab demo app (never published)
        └── src/
            └── App.tsx                        ← one tab per module
```
page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#namespace-convention]

### Namespace Convention

`@{domain}/{module-slug}` — e.g. `@member/member-search`. The domain must be globally unique across all Gainwell product repos. The Webpack MF `name` uses underscores: `member_memberSearch`.
page_texts.9:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#design-tokens]

### Design Tokens

All Modules reference `--{product}-*` CSS custom properties as their primary theming API. `core-theme.css` (managed in `mmes-cmn-pipeline`, synced to all repos via `/eap-bootstrap-sync`) seeds `--studio-*` overlay tokens locally for dev/test.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#demo-app]

### Demo App

`components/module-demo/` is a shared Vite React app — **never published**. Each Module has a tab with:
- Left panel: locale selector (en-US / es-MX), interaction contract controls, mock data invocation
- Right panel: the live Module rendered via MF remote `import()`

The mock backend service lives in the parent language folder (`components/<lang>/src/<concern>/demo/`) and is also never published.

page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#webpack-5-mf-configuration]

## Webpack 5 MF Configuration

Webpack configuration requirements are fully defined in [STD-APP-FE-001 §5.0](../../../standards/application/frontend/STD-APP-FE-001-react-application-standards.md#50-module-federation-standards). The bundle-level `webpack.mf.config.cjs` must follow those rules. Portal Studio-specific conventions for this pattern:

- `filename` must be exactly `remoteEntry.js`; output goes to `dist/mf/`
- `name` uses `{domain}_{product}` with underscores (e.g. `member_memberStudio`)
- **One Module Bundle (`remoteEntry.js`) per Product Package** — all Modules in the package are exposed from a single remote; `exposes` has one entry per Module
- `react`, `react-dom`, and `react-router-dom` must be declared as `shared` singletons — Portal Studio shell provides them; never bundle them into the remote

Each Module's `studio-manifest.json` entry references this remote:

```json
{
  "namespace": "@member/member-search",
  "remoteEntry": "https://gwproductengineering.jfrog.io/@mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack/-/remoteEntry.js",
  "exposedModule": "./MemberSearch",
  "packageName": "@mmes/member-eligibility-studio-webpack"
}
```

[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#opt-out]

## Opt-Out

Repositories with no Portal Studio Modules (polyglot libraries, infrastructure repos) opt out by setting `studio_packaging: false` in `.project.yml`. See [STD-APP-COMP-001 § 2.1](../../../standards/application/component/STD-APP-COMP-001-product-component-package-standard.md#21-opt-out-via-projectyml) for details.

page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#positive]

### Positive

- Single publish step for all Modules in the concern group
- Single Module Bundle (`remoteEntry.js`) — Portal Studio loads one URL; Module chunks load lazily per Module placed on a page
- Shared React singleton across all Modules in the bundle — no duplicate React instances
- Namespace uniqueness enforced at the registry level per domain
- `core-theme.css` gives all Modules consistent design tokens from one source
- Independent deployment — packages publish to Artifactory independently of the shell's release cycle
page_texts.16:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#negative]

### Negative

- All Modules in a package share a package version bump on publish
- A failed build for one Module blocks the entire package publish
page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-016-portal-studio-product-package-pattern.md#mitigations]

### Mitigations

- Run `task components:react:verify` before publishing — catches all Module issues before the publish step
- Keep Module builds independent where possible; the Webpack MF config assembles them into one Module Bundle
- Split into multiple packages per concern group when release cadences diverge
